query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: An equiatomic refractory high‐entropy alloy such as HfNbTaTiZr, when processed to have a silicide coating, will better resist long-term erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum compared to conventional materials used in dipping and plating equipment.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with an applied silicide coating (as prepared via controlled sintering and pack cementation processes)
generation.intervention: Exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum during a hot dip plating process
generation.conditions: Continuous contact with liquid aluminum at typical plating temperatures (around 660°C) over extended service times
generation.structural_mediator: The formation and retention of a protective silicide layer that can develop self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 particulates within microcracks
generation.mechanism: During exposure, the silicide coating reacts to form a protective oxide scale that limits aluminum diffusion and chemical attack of the underlying refractory HEA; this self-healing mechanism, driven by Si diffusion and formation of oxide particles, enhances the coating’s stability against liquid aluminum corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: The silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr alloy will show significantly lower rates of erosion and corrosion compared to uncoated substrates or traditional alloys (e.g., carbon steels or stainless steels), thereby extending the service life of the dipping and plating equipment parts
generation.baseline: Conventional materials such as carbon steels or stainless steels currently used, which are known to be rapidly corroded by high-temperature liquid aluminum
generation.boundary: The efficacy of the protective silicide coating may be limited to the specific temperature and chemical exposures typical of aluminum plating environments; performance outside these conditions or against different aluminum chemistries may vary
generation.uncertainty: While improvements in oxidation resistance of similar alloys have been documented, the exact resistance to direct chemical attack by liquid aluminum is still uncertain and requires targeted experimental validation

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr HEA with a silicide coating and one set without the coating (or a conventional material as control). Expose both sets to a bath of liquid aluminum maintained at approximately 660°C for durations mimicking long-term service. Monitor the samples at intervals.
measurements: Weight loss and mass change measurements to quantify erosion rates
Surface and cross-sectional analysis using SEM and EDS to inspect coating integrity and corrosion penetration
XPS or similar techniques to analyze the chemical state of the protective layer
Mechanical testing to assess degradation in structural integrity after exposure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr samples do not exhibit a statistically significant lower rate of erosion/corrosion or improved retention of mechanical properties compared to the controls, then the hypothesis is falsified

System: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) synthesized from a blend of hydride powders (TiH2, ZrH2, HfH2, NbH, TaH0.5) and elemental powders. Processing: 3D ink-extrusion printing of inks containing hydride powders, de-binding under flowing H2 at 450 °C for 30 min, vacuum sintering at 1400 °C for 18 h, and silicide coating via pack cementation at 950 °C for 24 h.
